title: TAP Dev Passkey Record
description: The PUBLIC credential record a developer exports once (after registering a localhost passkey) so every freshly-spawned dev session can bind that same passkey with no re-registration (req-tap-auth-passkey-dev-bootstrap). Contains ONLY public material — never the private key, which stays under the authenticator/platform. CONFIDENTIALITY IS LOW-STAKES (reading this grants nothing); INTEGRITY IS LOAD-BEARING: import substitutes file bytes for the registration ceremony's proof-of-possession, so whoever controls these bytes controls which public key becomes admin. The record is written 0600 in an operator-owned dir (the named load-bearing mitigation) and carries a self-digest for corruption detection; the dev/local allowlist gate (req-tap-auth-passkey-dev-bootstrap-4) bounds blast radius. Schema validation checks SHAPE, not authenticity.

version.description: Record schema version. 1 for the v0 shape.

rp_id.description: The Relying Party ID the credential is scoped to. In v0 this is ALWAYS `localhost`: WebAuthn's http secure-context carve-out is host `localhost`, and RP-ID `localhost` (which ignores port) is what lets one credential span every session's stack. A record with any other rp_id is refused.

origin_policy.description: How the login origin is resolved at import/login time. ALWAYS `per_session_localhost_exact`: the expected origin is NOT baked into this shared record — each importing session enforces its OWN exact origin `http://localhost:<its WEB_PORT>` (scheme+host+port), taken from that session's settings. This is the only thing preventing a co-resident `localhost:<other>` service from relaying a TAP-challenge assertion; a baked-in or any-`localhost` wildcard origin would open that relay (req-tap-auth-passkey-dev-bootstrap-6). Recorded here as a described constant so the policy travels with the file, not as a concrete origin.

user_handle.description: The opaque WebAuthn user handle (hex) the ORIGINAL registration used as `user.id` — captured once and replayed so every session's imported admin shares this handle and the discoverable credential on the authenticator resolves consistently (autofill). NOT a secret; it identifies which discoverable credential to offer, not proof of anything.

credential.description: The public credential material captured from the registered WebAuthnCredential.

credential_id.description: The globally-unique credential id (base64url). The authenticator returns this on assertion; import binds it so a later assertion resolves to the imported admin.

public_key.description: The COSE-encoded public key (base64url). The public half used to verify assertion signatures; the private half is never exported.

sign_count.description: The signature counter captured at export (0 for platform passkeys, which do not increment). Imported as the stored baseline; because a real authenticator's counter only advances, a fresh session's assertion never regresses below this — so replay across sessions is safe (req-tap-auth-passkey-webauthn-8).

aaguid.description: The authenticator AAGUID (UUID string; all-zeros = unknown under attestation none). Public, informational.

transports.description: The transports the authenticator advertised (e.g. `internal`, `hybrid`). Public hint.

device_type.description: Whether the credential is device-bound (`single_device`) or multi-device/synced (`multi_device`) — derived from the BE flag at registration. Feeds recovery-risk legibility, not authorization.

backed_up.description: The Backup State (BS) flag at registration — whether the credential is currently backed up / synced. Public characteristic.

exported_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp the record was exported. Informational only; not part of the integrity digest's authority (it is inside the digested content, but the digest is corruption-detection, not authenticity).

integrity.description: Corruption-detection self-digest. `digest` is the sha256 (hex) of the CANONICAL record with this `integrity` object removed. It catches accidental truncation/corruption and pins the shape; it is NOT anti-tamper against a same-uid process (which could recompute it) — that residual is the NAMED load-bearing risk the 0600 + operator-owned-dir mitigation covers (req-tap-auth-passkey-dev-bootstrap-8).

digest_alg.description: The digest algorithm. Always `sha256` in v0.

digest.description: Lowercase-hex sha256 of the canonical record (sorted keys, tight separators) with the `integrity` key removed.
